newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw upgraded to outperform by DLJ.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw upgraded to outperform by DLJ.

text.p: Waste management and transportation firm Laidlaw Inc was upgraded to outperform from market perform by U.S. brokerage Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette on Monday, analyst Marc Sulam said.
"I think you've got limited downside with potential for some interesting upside opportunities," Sulam told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Sulam said that among reasons for the upgrade was that Canadian Pacific Ltd, Laidlaw's largest shareholder, was considering selling its 47 percent voting stake.
Sulam gave Laidlaw stock a one-year price target of C$12 to C$14 in his report. Laidlaw rose 0.20 to 13.55 on more than half a million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange in late trading.

"We believe that (CP) has unsuccessfully attempted to shop its stake several times over the past several years, but has become more interested in monetizing its investment," Sulam said in his report. "While stressing that CP's intentions have not been announced, we think a one-two year timetable to clarify and resolve this issue is realistic and would represent a positive for the stock," he added.
Sulam forecast that Laidlaw would see "over the course of the next 12-24 months an acceleration of earnings growth in fiscal 1997 and 1998."

Sulam said income would rise as Laidlaw benefited from its acquisition of the transportation unit of Scott's Hospitality Inc in August and a growing trend for the healthcare business to outsource its transportation needs.

Since Laidlaw had several different businesses, "I think Laidlaw is a fairly misunderstood company and stock, especially in the U.S.," Sulam said. Laidlaw is mostly covered by environmental industry analysts.

Laidlaw shares rose last week on Canadian market rumors that Republic Industries Inc was set to buy Laidlaw's solid waste management component for US$1 million. The rumor was denied by both companies.
"I doubt that that's going to happen," Sulam said.
